root.name: Benko Gambit: Nescafe Frappe Attack
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 c5 3. d5 b5 4. cxb5 a6 5. Nc3 axb5 6. e4 b4 7. Nb5 d6 8. Bc4

overview: In the Zaitsev Benko, White has taken the b-pawn, played e4 and put a knight on b5, here followed by Bc4 with ideas of Nxd6+ tricks and pressure on f7. Black is a pawn down for open a- and b-files and play against the queenside, and must meet the knight's threats on d6 and c7. I am not sure of the exact theory of this named line.

white_ideas.idea: Use the active Nb5 and Bc4 to pressure d6 and f7
Complete development with Nf3, O-O and Bf4 or Bg5

black_ideas.idea: Stay a pawn down for queenside pressure on the a- and b-files

typical_structures.structure: Benko queenside structure with open a- and b-files
White central pawns on d5 and e4

character.notes: Benko lines trade a pawn for long queenside pressure, and this line adds early tactics around d6 and f7.

gambit.notes: Black gave the b-pawn and White can keep it, though Black has long compensation.

soundness.notes: The Benko is sound; this side line is not known to be a refutation.

structure.notes: Open a- and b-files for Black with a fixed d5 pawn; half-open files.

approach.notes: A normal Benko line, standard for those who play the gambit.

level.notes: Concrete tactics around Nb5 must be known and the compensation is positional.

character.reason: A pawn gambit with concrete tactics around d6 and f7.
